about.description:
pyscal computes descriptors of the local atomic structure from atomistic
simulation data, such as Steinhardt parameters, common neighbor analysis,
Voronoi tessellation and many more. It works on ASE Atoms objects. The
calculations run in C++ on all CPU cores, with Python bindings through
pybind11. It includes the C++ core of matscipy-neighbours (MIT) for the
neighbor search.
about.summary: Calculation of local atomic structural environments from atomistic simulation data

commands: python -c "from ase.build import bulk; import pyscal3; a = bulk('Cu', 'fcc', a=3.61, cubic=True).repeat(3); assert pyscal3.common_neighbor_analysis(a)['fcc'] == len(a)"

raw_meta_yaml:
{% set name = "pyscal3" %}
{% set version = "4.1.0" %}

package:
  name: {{ name|lower }}
  version: {{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/pyscal/{{ name }}/archive/{{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 83dd6fa9a675a8c3babd6499f032ae6a5f4bba536ff0a6ac97018dc962308836

build:
  number: 0
  skip: true  # [py<310]
  script: {{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation

requirements:
  build:
    - python                                 # [build_platform != target_platform]
    - cross-python_{{ target_platform }}     # [build_platform != target_platform]
    - pybind11 >=2.12                        # [build_platform != target_platform]
    - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
    - {{ stdlib("c") }}
  host:
    - python
    - pip
    - setuptools >=64
    - wheel
    - pybind11 >=2.12
  run:
    - python
    - numpy
    - scipy >=1.15
    - ase
    - pyyaml

test:
  imports:
    - pyscal3
    - pyscal
  requires:
    - pip
  commands:
    - pip check
    - python -c "from ase.build import bulk; import pyscal3; a = bulk('Cu', 'fcc', a=3.61, cubic=True).repeat(3); assert pyscal3.common_neighbor_analysis(a)['fcc'] == len(a)"

about:
  home: https://pyscal.org
  license: BSD-3-Clause AND MIT
  license_family: BSD
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - lib/matscipy-neighbours/LICENSE.md
  summary: Calculation of local atomic structural environments from atomistic simulation data
  description: |
    pyscal computes descriptors of the local atomic structure from atomistic
    simulation data, such as Steinhardt parameters, common neighbor analysis,
    Voronoi tessellation and many more. It works on ASE Atoms objects. The
    calculations run in C++ on all CPU cores, with Python bindings through
    pybind11. It includes the C++ core of matscipy-neighbours (MIT) for the
    neighbor search.
  doc_url: https://pyscal.org
  dev_url: https://github.com/pyscal/pyscal3/

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - srmnitc
